column1: Polar bears are being increasingly threatened by the effects of climate change, but their disappearance could have far-reaching consequences.
column2: 气候变化的影响正使北极熊面临越来越大的威胁，而这一物种的消失可能带来深远的后果。

column1: They are uniquely adapted to the extreme conditions of the Arctic Circle, where temperatures can reach −40°C.
column2: 北极圈的气温可低至−40°C，北极熊有着独特的本领，能够适应那里的极端条件。

column1: One reason for this is that they have up to 11 centimetres of fat underneath their skin.
column2: 原因之一是，它们皮下的脂肪层可厚达11厘米。

column1: Humans with comparative levels of adipose tissue would be considered obese and would be likely to suffer from diabetes and heart disease.
column2: 人类若有相近含量的脂肪组织，就会被视为肥胖，而且很可能患上糖尿病和心脏病。

column1: Yet the polar bear experiences no such consequences.
column2: 但北极熊却不会出现这样的后果。

column1: A 2014 study by Shi Ping Liu and colleagues sheds light on this mystery.
column2: Shi Ping Liu及其同事在2014年开展的一项研究为解开这一谜团提供了线索。
column5: sheds light on|为理解……提供线索

column1: They compared the genetic structure of polar bears with that of their closest relatives from a warmer climate, the brown bears.
column2: 他们比较了北极熊和棕熊的遗传结构。棕熊是北极熊亲缘关系最近的动物，生活在气候较温暖的地方。
column5: closest relatives|亲缘关系最近的物种

column1: This allowed them to determine the genes that have allowed polar bears to survive in one of the toughest environments on Earth.
column2: 通过比较，他们得以确定哪些基因让北极熊能够在地球上最严酷的环境之一生存。

column1: Liu and his colleagues found the polar bears had a gene known as APoB, which reduces levels of low-density lipoproteins (LDLs) — a form of ‘bad’ cholesterol.
column2: Liu和同事发现，北极熊有一种名为APoB的基因，能降低低密度脂蛋白（LDL）的水平。低密度脂蛋白是一种“坏”胆固醇。

column1: In humans, mutations of this gene are associated with increased risk of heart disease.
column2: 在人类身上，这种基因的突变与心脏病风险增加有关。

column1: Polar bears may therefore be an important study model to understand heart disease in humans.
column2: 因此，北极熊可能是人们研究人类心脏病的重要模型。

column1: The genome of the polar bear may also provide the solution for another condition, one that particularly affects our older generation: osteoporosis.
column2: 北极熊的基因组也可能为解决另一种病症提供办法，那就是对老年人影响尤大的骨质疏松症。

column1: This is a disease where bones show reduced density, usually caused by insufficient exercise, reduced calcium intake or food starvation.
column2: 这种病的表现是骨密度降低，通常是由于运动不足、钙摄入量减少或缺少食物。
column7: food starvation|食物匮乏所致的饥饿

column1: Bone tissue is constantly being remodelled, meaning that bone is added or removed, depending on nutrient availability and the stress that the bone is under.
column2: 骨组织一直在重塑，也就是说，骨质会生成或被吸收，具体取决于能获得多少营养，以及骨骼承受多大负荷。
column7: nutrient availability|营养物质的可获得量

column1: Female polar bears, however, undergo extreme conditions during every pregnancy.
column2: 然而，雌性北极熊每次怀孕都会经历极端的条件。

column1: Once autumn comes around, these females will dig maternity dens in the snow and will remain there throughout the winter, both before and after the birth of their cubs.
column2: 秋天一到，雌熊就会在雪中挖产仔用的洞穴，在幼崽出生前后都待在里面，整个冬季都是如此。

column1: This process results in about six months of fasting, where the female bears have to keep themselves and their cubs alive, depleting their own calcium and calorie reserves.
column2: 这意味着它们要禁食约六个月。雌熊在这期间必须维持自己和幼崽的生命，为此不断消耗自身储备的钙和能量。
column5: keep themselves and their cubs alive|维持自己和幼崽的生命

column1: Despite this, their bones remain strong and dense.
column2: 尽管如此，它们的骨骼依然坚固致密。

column1: Physiologists Alanda Lennox and Allen Goodship found an explanation for this paradox in 2008.
column2: 2008年，生理学家阿兰达·伦诺克斯和艾伦·古德希普为这个看似矛盾的现象找到了解释。

column1: They discovered that pregnant bears were able to increase the density of their bones before they started to build their dens.
column2: 他们发现，怀孕的北极熊在开始挖洞穴之前，就能够提高骨密度。

column1: In addition, six months later, when they finally emerged from the den with their cubs, there was no evidence of significant loss of bone density.
column2: 此外，六个月后，雌熊最终带着幼崽走出洞穴时，也没有证据表明骨密度出现了显著下降。

column1: Hibernating brown bears do not have this capacity and must therefore resort to major bone reformation in the following spring.
column2: 冬眠的棕熊不具备这种能力，因此到第二年春天，必须依靠大规模的骨组织重建。

column1: If the mechanism of bone remodelling in polar bears can be understood, many bedridden humans, and even astronauts, could potentially benefit.
column2: 如果能弄清北极熊骨重塑的机制，许多卧床不起的病人，甚至宇航员，都有可能从中受益。

column1: The medical benefits of the polar bear for humanity certainly have their importance in our conservation efforts, but these should not be the only factors taken into consideration.
column2: 在保护北极熊时，它可能为人类医学带来的益处当然值得重视，但我们考虑的因素不应仅限于此。

column1: We tend to want to protect animals we think are intelligent and possess emotions, such as elephants and primates.
column2: 我们往往愿意保护自己认为有智慧、有情感的动物，如大象和灵长类动物。

column1: Bears, on the other hand, seem to be perceived as stupid and in many cases violent.
column2: 另一方面，人们似乎认为熊很笨，而且有许多熊很凶猛。
column3: on the other hand|另一方面
column6: in many cases|在很多情况下
column7: violent|adj. 凶猛的；具有攻击性的

column1: And yet anecdotal evidence from the field challenges those assumptions, suggesting for example that polar bears have good problem-solving abilities.
column2: 然而，野外的零星观察对这些看法提出了挑战。例如，有些观察提示，北极熊具有很好的解决问题的能力。
column3: anecdotal evidence|零星观察所得的证据

column1: A male bear called GoGo in Tennoji Zoo, Osaka, has even been observed making use of a tool to manipulate his environment.
column2: 在大阪天王寺动物园，人们甚至观察到一只名叫GoGo的雄性北极熊使用工具改变周围的环境。

column1: The bear used a tree branch on multiple occasions to dislodge a piece of meat hung out of his reach.
column2: 这只熊多次用树枝把挂在自己够不到的地方的一块肉拨落。
column7: out of his reach|在够不到的地方

column1: Problem-solving ability has also been witnessed in wild polar bears, although not as obviously as with GoGo.
column2: 人们也观察到野生北极熊具有解决问题的能力，只是表现得没有GoGo那么明显。

column1: A calculated move by a male bear involved running and jumping onto barrels in an attempt to get to a photographer standing on a platform four metres high.
column2: 一只雄熊曾有意跑过去跳上桶，试图够到一位站在四米高的平台上的摄影师。

column1: In other studies, such as one by Alison Ames in 2008, polar bears showed deliberate and focussed manipulation.
column2: 在其他研究中，例如艾莉森·埃姆斯2008年的一项研究，北极熊表现出了有意识且专注地操弄物体的行为。

column1: For example, Ames observed bears putting objects in piles and then knocking them over in what appeared to be a game.
column2: 例如，埃姆斯观察到熊把一些东西堆起来，然后又将它们推倒，像是在玩游戏。

column1: The study demonstrates that bears are capable of agile and thought-out behaviours.
column2: 这项研究表明，熊能够做出灵活、经过思考的行为。

column1: These examples suggest bears have greater creativity and problem-solving abilities than previously thought.
column2: 这些例子表明，熊的创造力和解决问题的能力，比人们以前所认为的更强。

column1: As for emotions, while the evidence is once again anecdotal, many bears have been seen to hit out at ice and snow — seemingly out of frustration — when they have just missed out on a kill.
column2: 说到情感，证据也仍然来自零星观察；人们见过许多北极熊在刚刚错失猎物后朝冰雪拍打，似乎在发泄挫败感。

column1: Moreover, polar bears can form unusual relationships with other species, including playing with the dogs used to pull sleds in the Arctic.
column2: 此外，北极熊能与其他物种建立不同寻常的关系，例如同北极地区用来拉雪橇的狗玩耍。

column1: Remarkably, one hand-raised polar bear called Agee has formed a close relationship with her owner Mark Dumas to the point where they even swim together.
column2: 更令人瞩目的是，一只名叫Agee、由人养大的北极熊与饲主马克·杜马斯关系密切，甚至能一起游泳。
column7: to the point where|达到……的程度

column1: This is even more astonishing since polar bears are known to actively hunt humans in the wild.
column2: 这就更令人吃惊了，因为人们知道，野生北极熊会主动猎食人类。

column1: If climate change were to lead to their extinction, this would mean not only the loss of potential breakthroughs in human medicine, but more importantly, the disappearance of an intelligent, majestic animal.
column2: 如果气候变化真的导致北极熊灭绝，人类医学就会失去一些取得突破的可能；更重要的是，一种聪慧而威严的动物也会从此消失。
